# Analyse the folder structure

Focus, if given: $ARGUMENTS

Follow `.claude/rules/how-to-use-sdlc-docs.md`. Edit only `docs/sdlc/01-folder-structure.md`.

## 1. Map the tree

Use Glob to list folders up to 3 levels deep. Skip folders that are generated, downloaded or tool-specific:
`.git`, `node_modules`, `target`, `build`, `dist`, `out`, `bin`, `obj`, `.gradle`, `.idea`, `.vscode`,
`venv`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `coverage`, `.next`, `.nuxt`, `vendor`, `.terraform`.

## 2. Understand each important folder

For every top-level folder and the main folders inside the source and test roots, work out:

- What lives there: read the folder name, file names, and one or two representative files.
- Whether it's source, tests, config, build/CI, infrastructure, docs, static assets or generated output.
- Entry points: main classes, `index`/`main` files, app bootstrap, route definitions.

Also work out:

- Languages, frameworks and versions, from the build files.
- Architecture style: layered (controller/service/repository), feature folders, hexagonal, MVC, monorepo
  packages, etc. Say what you see, with an example path.
- Where each kind of new code belongs: a new endpoint, service, data model, UI page or component, test, config
  value, database migration. Base this on where existing examples of the same kind live.

## 3. Update `docs/sdlc/01-folder-structure.md`

- Keep any text a person wrote. Fill empty sections and update earlier INFERRED sections.
- Tree: at most about 60 lines. Collapse big or repetitive folders, e.g. `components/  (48 React components)`.
- Mark every section you write with `<!-- INFERRED: folder scan, <date> -->`.
- This file loads in every session, so keep it under about 120 lines.

## 4. Return a summary

Reply in at most 15 lines: the architecture style, the main source and test roots, entry points, anything
surprising (duplicate folders, dead code, generated files committed to the repo), and what you changed.
